newsitem.title: DUBAI: Visa says credit cards catching on in the Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Visa says credit cards catching on in the Gulf.

text.p: Spending on Visa credit cards in the Gulf jumped 81 percent to 16.15 billion dirhams ($4.4 billion) in the year to end-March 1997, the Gulf Today newspaper reported on Sunday.
It quoted Visa regional director Peter Scriven as saying there were 1.45 million cardholders in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar.

"Clearly, plastic money is fast catching on but we still have a long way to go. For instance, credit card purchases in the UAE represent only three percent of the total, implying 97 percent of purchases are still transacted in cash," he said.
Scriven said UAE cardholders spent 5.98 billion dirhams in the year to end-March -- a 72 percent increase. In Saudi Arabia they spent 12 percent more at 4.4 billion dirhams.
Kuwaiti cardholders spent 4.6 billion dirhams -- 328 percent up on the year -- and Qatari and Omani visa cardholders spent 680 million and 76.55 million dirhams respectively.
The newspaper said Visa had undertaken two Gulf promotions to try to break the region's cash habit.
"The stress is not on encouraging overspending but to replace cash transactions with plastic money," Scriven said.
